event: Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. common stock listed for trading on the New York Stock Exchange
notes: verbatim: 'August 25, 1972, the Company's stock was listed and began trading on the New York Stock Exchange'; OTC since October 1970. NEW contemporaneous fact the five downloads produced

event: Arthur Young & Company signs the unqualified report on the consolidated statements for the year ended January 31, 1974
notes: first of five newly-witnessed opinions

event: A new 150,000 square foot Distribution Center begins operation in Bentonville, consolidating case-pack merchandise previously shipped direct to stores
notes: 8 rail-car and 37 truck doors against the original DC's 6 and 28; ~60% of merchandise shipped through warehouse/DC in FY1975 vs 55% the prior year

event: Arthur Young qualifies its FY1975 opinion by exception for the change in the method of determining inventory cost (FIFO to LIFO), an change the auditor states it approves
notes: the comparability break in the margin series is auditor-flagged, not footnoted: FY1975 earnings fall $2,347,000 ($.36 pre-split, $.18 post-split)

event: A second 150,000 square foot Bentonville distribution centre is completed, making 300,000 sq ft of 'pure distribution center' on a two-and-one-half-day cycle
notes: total Bentonville distribution ≈550,000 sq ft through which ~80% of merchandise flows, up from 60% two years earlier

event: Arthur Young & Company signs the unqualified FY1977 report; wording has moved from 'consistent with that of the preceding year' to 'applied on a consistent basis during the period'
notes: the opinion now covers two years

event: Construction begins on a 390,000 square foot distribution center at Searcy, Arkansas, designed to service one-half of the existing stores
notes: automated conveyor at ~200 ft/min; combines DC I warehousing with DC II distribution; completion then tentative for June 1978

event: A group of sixteen stores is acquired in late summer, four stores closed during FY1978 including two of the acquired units
notes: the only store-group acquisition in the window stated in its own year's report; identity of the seller is not given in the FY1978 report

event: Arthur Young & Company signs the unqualified FY1978 report
notes: the FY1978 report is the cleanest text layer of the five new documents and A3's reference copy for FY1970-FY1978

event: The remaining Sav-Co Home Improvement Center is closed, ending the nine-year second-format experiment begun in FY1975
notes: FY1975 opened two Sav-Co centres totalling 54,000 sq ft and already conceded they 'will not be expanded until [they are] operating at our expected profitability level'

event: Arthur Young signs the FY1979 report carrying the clause that prior-year statements were restated retroactively for the change in the method of accounting for leases (SFAS 13), a change the auditor concurs in
notes: the authorising document for the restatement of FY1975-FY1978 — a second restating document one year earlier than A2's only one

event: Sam M. Walton opens his first Ben Franklin franchise variety store in Newport, Arkansas — as narrated by the registrant in 1974, 1975, 1977, 1978 and 1979
notes: NO 1945 document exists in this corpus; five dated repeatings inside ONE lineage do not make a second source (§3 filing-lineage rule)

event: The first Wal-Mart Discount City opens in Rogers, Arkansas, a town of 'approximately 4700' (FY1975) / 'approximately 5,000 people' (FY1978)
actors: Sam M. Walton; J. L. 'Bud' Walton
notes: the month is stated in the FY1975 and FY1978 reports; no 1962 price, no opening-day takings, and no witness outside the registrant

event: The variety/soft-goods trade's own journal reports that the spread of discount houses is 'slowing down' (28% more / 6% fewer / 66% no change among responding member stores)
notes: SECTOR context four years before the first Wal-Mart Discount City. Evidence that a 1962 entrant was entering a sector its own trade journal was already describing as saturating — market-as-knowable, NOT a company claim.

event: NRMA (the renamed NRDGA, Walton's own franchise association) holds its first Discount Seminar, 'The Discount Business — Is It for You?', ~800 attendees, half conventional department stores
actors: National Retail Merchants Association; J. Gordon Dakins; Milton Woll; Richard Tumpowsky (American Dixie Shops); Perry Meyers; Stephen Masters; Alfred C. Thompson; Manfred Brecker (S. E. Nichols Co.)
notes: Reported in the December 1961 issue, three months before the first Wal-Mart opened. The trade formalised the discount transition before and independently of the company.

event: S. E. Nichols Company is described as operator of 'Nichols Discount Cities since 1958, and with a long previous history in variety stores'
notes: A VARIETY-TO-DISCOUNT PRECEDENT printed in the company's own trade journal before the company existed. Anti-hagiography service (§2): it makes the registrant's later origin narrative one instance of a trade-wide move rather than an unprecedented act.

event: 'Discounters invade food field: And supermarkets are fighting back' (with illus) p.62
notes: INDEX-LEVEL ONLY: headline, page, date. No article text is reachable for 1962 on this route, so nothing about its content is asserted anywhere in A4.

event: 'Discounter caught in cash bind: Grayson-Robinson's plight may presage a discount house shakeout' p.109 (OCR also prints p.169)
notes: Page number unresolved between printings of the same OCR layer; both readings recorded, neither chosen. Sector, not company.

event: 'Discount store dropouts' p.101 — a short item on discount-store exits, within months of the first Wal-Mart opening
notes: Same calendar year as the Rogers opening; BW indexed exits, not the new entrant. The absence is the record: A4-01, A4-17.

event: 'Shake-out among discounters seen as chain files in bankruptcy' p.83
notes: Sector consolidation by failure, indexed in the founding year.

event: 'Discounters strive to ride out storm: fast-growing $6-billion industry is facing a major shakeout' p.78
notes: Carries the $6-billion sector figure. Disagrees with BW's own July 1963 report of $6.9 billion for calendar 1962; both kept.

event: Short item: discount stores amounted to $6.9 billion in 1962, p.132
notes: The fragment is legible; the printed subject noun and universe are lost to OCR reflow. Recorded, not reconciled.

event: 'Survey by Dun & Bradstreet shows that … and television are the most profitable departments in a sampling of discount stores' p.79
notes: A NON-COMPANY SURVEY OF THE TRADE, now dated and paginated. The D&B volume itself is UNTRIED. This is the genre A3 §7.2(d) asked for, as a count of the industry rather than of the company — so it does not move the company's lineage count.

event: 'Fewer stores to share the pie: They get bigger but decrease in number as discounters, chains squeeze little guys' p.182
notes: Independent sector statement that the discount-store COUNT WAS FALLING in Wal-Mart's second year. Sector universes differ from the registrant's unit series; no reconciliation attempted.

event: 'Nielsen survey shows an increase in the number of mass merchandisers' p.100
actors: A. C. Nielsen via Business Week
notes: Third-party counting operation on the mass-merchandiser population. Counterevidence to the 1963 'fewer stores' headline; different definitions of the counted class, so neither is preferred.

event: 'Small town greets the discounters' p.90 — indexed under ALDENS, Inc.; the cross-entry reads 'Gamble-Skogmo is opening franchised …'
actors: Business Week; Aldens Inc.; Gamble-Skogmo Inc.
notes: THE DOSSIER'S MOST DANGEROUS FALSE POSITIVE: a headline that reads like Wal-Mart's own positioning, belonging to two Minnesota-based variety/mail-order operators. Not Wal-Mart evidence at any confidence. COR-A4-06.

event: 'The old five-and-ten spreads new wings: Woolworth branches out into mass merchandising in varied lines' (with cover and illus) p.58
actors: F. W. Woolworth Co. via Business Week
notes: The largest incumbent variety chain publicly entering discount mass-merchandising — the same conversion path, at the top of the industry, in Wal-Mart's second year.

event: Short item: Woolworth 'is setting up Worth Marts, discount mass-volume stores' p.24
notes: Named-format evidence of the variety-to-discount conversion.

event: 'Is the franchise system legal? Supreme Court answer[ed] … when it decides GM violated Sherman Act' p.66
notes: Franchise-law question bearing on the Ben Franklin form. Article text UNREACHABLE, so the legal content is not asserted; the index entry is the whole fact.

event: 'Is success spoiling discount stores? Moves to carry more costly merchandise worry industry leaders' (with illus) p.97
notes: Sector self-doubt indexed three years after Wal-Mart's founding.

event: 'Helping a small town cope with prosperity' (with illus) p.184 — a Jones & Laughlin steel-mill town story (Hennepin, Illinois)
notes: Fifth documented decoy on the 'small town' theme. Recorded so no later pass reads BW's small-town coverage as Wal-Mart's.

event: 'Discount stores getting tryout' p.98; and 1969-09-20 'A discounter is a Washington department store' p.108
notes: Sector spread into new markets in the year before Wal-Mart's OTC listing.

event: 'How Kresge became top discounter' (with cover, chart and illus) p.62 — cross-indexed under DISCOUNT Houses, KRESGE (S. S.) Co. AND VARIETY Stores
actors: S. S. Kresge Co. via Business Week
notes: Third-party naming of Wal-Mart's principal comparator, and BW's own taxonomy placing Kresge under VARIETY Stores is independent evidence that the variety and discount trades were publicly treated as one competitive field in Wal-Mart's first public year.

event: 'France: The French go wild over discount stores' (with illus) p.40
notes: Sector framing by 1971 is international; the discount model was a general business phenomenon, not an American teleology pointing at one chain.

event: NO independent periodical witness naming Wal-Mart recovered for ANY year of Stage 1
notes: The verdict-bearing row. 0 of 19 years. It is a statement about the corpus reachable from this machine plus three blocked host families (family 3 UNANSWERED in part), NOT a statement that no such print exists.

event: *Stores* monthly issues sampled contain no mention of Walton's, Wal-Mart, Ben Franklin Stores, Bentonville or Springdale
notes: 7 of ~200 issues. The journal's genre (management and policy, not directory) is the probable reason and is stated as an INFERENCE with an alternative explanation, not as proof (A4-29).

actors: HathiTrust; Google Books; A4 re-probe pass
